title: Body Control Module Internal Fault
shortDescription: BCM reports an internal logic, RAM, or ROM fault.
fullDescription: DTC B2000: BCM reports an internal logic, RAM, or ROM fault. Body B-codes in the B2000–B3500 range cover BCM internals, doors, lighting, SRS/airbag, climate, immobilizer, and comfort accessories.
safetyImpact: Body / comfort fault. Vehicle remains drivable but the affected accessory may not function.

causes.cause: Blown fuse on the affected circuit

symptoms: Affected accessory not working
Warning light or message in cluster
Battery drain if circuit stays active
Intermittent operation
Multiple related comfort features failing together

fixSteps.title: Scan Body Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool that supports body modules (BCM, RCM, climate, immobilizer) to pull all stored codes.

fixSteps.title: Check Fuses and Power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the fuse(s) for the affected circuit, then confirm power and ground at the connector.

fixSteps.title: Test Component Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Command the actuator on/off via scan tool and measure response. For airbag/SRS circuits, follow proper safety lockout procedures.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Program
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed component. Program / configure to the BCM if required.

faq.q: Is a body code dangerous?
faq.a: Most body codes are comfort-related and safe to drive with. SRS / airbag / pretensioner codes (B2300–B2430) are safety-critical and should be repaired immediately.

faq.q: Why do I have several body codes at once?
faq.a: Body codes often share power, ground, or BCM drivers — a single connector or fuse can trip many codes.

faq.q: Can I work on airbag circuits myself?
faq.a: Disconnect the battery and wait the manufacturer-specified time before touching SRS components. When in doubt, leave it to a shop.

faq.q: Is a body code dangerous?

faq.q: Why do I have several body codes at once?
faq.a: Body codes often share power, ground, or BCM drivers — a single connector or fuse can trip many codes.

faq.q: Can I work on airbag circuits myself?
faq.a: Disconnect the battery and wait the manufacturer-specified time before touching SRS components. When in doubt, leave it to a shop.
